block.gpio.apply_hint: Changes remain local until Apply. Restart a loaded Run to use new settings.
block.gpio.invalid_number: Check the numeric value and its limits.
block.gpio.model.title: Button & LED
block.gpio.model.description: Debounced Linux GPIO button events and bounded low-voltage LED commands through installed libgpiod 2.x.
block.gpio.help_enabled: Off by default. Only buttons and indicator LEDs with correct current limiting; never mains, power relays or safety-critical devices.
block.gpio.help_chip: Exact /dev/gpiochipN from the installed board. Offsets below are chip line offsets, not physical header pin numbers.
block.gpio.help_button_offset: -1 disables the button. Choose an unused input line and verify the board pinout before enabling.
block.gpio.help_led_offset: -1 disables the LED. Must differ from the button. Use a resistor and respect the board's voltage/current ratings.
block.gpio.help_button_active_low: Checked means a low electrical level is a press. Startup and resume establish a baseline; they do not invent a press.
block.gpio.help_button_bias: Internal bias is best effort in Linux. Provide the required external bias; a floating input is not reliable.
block.gpio.help_debounce_ms: Emit only after the sampled level remains stable. Held buttons do not repeat; very short pulses may be missed.
block.gpio.help_led_active_low: Checked means logical on drives a low electrical level. Verify the circuit; this does not change the supply voltage.
block.gpio.label_rest_active: LED on at rest / before release
block.gpio.help_rest_active: Applied at acquisition, after timed patterns and before release. After release or power loss the circuit, not this block, determines the level.
block.gpio.help_max_pattern_ms: Every on command needs duration_ms. Blink count and complete duration are bounded. A new accepted command replaces the current pattern.
block.gpio.help_max_events_per_run: Releases the lines at this limit. Pause/resume does not reset the total; start a new Run.
block.gpio.help_poll_interval_ms: Ordinary human buttons, not pulse counting or real-time control. Scheduling delays can miss short transitions.
block.gpio.help_library: Normally libgpiod.so.3 (API 2.x). An absolute .so path loads native code: only use a trusted installed library.
